note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: Wall Street just endorsed Jensen Huang's 'big concept' for AI. What now?
items.blurb: Six asset managers backing Nvidia's plan treat AI compute as a financeable asset class, not a depreciating capex line.

items.title: Why Intel's selling new stock
items.blurb: Intel is issuing equity into a 150% year-to-date run, funding fab expansion off AI-driven chip demand.

items.title: Manus to return as independent company after China forced Meta to unwind $2 billion deal
items.blurb: Chinese regulators unwound Meta's agent-startup acquisition, showing Beijing will block outbound AI deals on national grounds.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Glimmer open-weight AI model
items.blurb: Meta open-sources a 30B model built to run on laptops, shifting agent workloads off cloud data centers.

items.title: Exclusive: Sanders calls for AI development pause
items.blurb: Sanders asks Altman, Amodei and Zuckerberg to pause development, warning Congress will act if labs do not.

items.title: House Dems call for AI companies to testify on recent hacks: 'Clear risk to safety'
items.blurb: Lawmakers want AI chief executives under oath after a run of model-driven hacking incidents.

items.title: Intel plans $15 billion stock offering as AI demand accelerates
items.blurb: Intel raises equity to fund AI compute capacity as sector capex tracks toward $765 billion this year.

items.title: I caught my students using AI to cheat in an exam — here's what universities must do to stamp this out
items.blurb: A Brown University economics exam becomes a case study in how assessment breaks under widely available AI.

items.title: World's biggest chipmaker TSMC's sales surge 45% amid buoyant AI demand
items.blurb: July revenue rose 44.7% year over year, with high-performance computing at 66% of sales — AI demand still accelerating.

items.title: The Download: AI agents for science, and the "censorship-industrial complex"
items.blurb: Schmidt Sciences argues AI agents can accelerate discovery; a Texas Amazon data center is permitted for 33 million tons of CO2.

items.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6-Cyber to help prepare for AI cyberattacks
items.blurb: OpenAI ships a deliberately less-restricted cyber model to vetted defenders, its first rated High-capability under the Preparedness Framework.

items.title: AI for science needs reasoning, not just data
items.blurb: Argues research agents that model the scientific process, not just pattern-match data, are what will actually accelerate discovery.

items.title: Nvidia teams up with Wall Street asset managers on $500 billion AI infrastructure push
items.blurb: Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman and KKR join Nvidia to mobilize third-party capital for data centers and chip purchases.

items.title: When will we see profits from the AI buildout?
items.blurb: Four years into the boom, earnings reports still do not disclose returns on hyperscalers' AI infrastructure spending.

items.title: These startups are chasing the next big thing in LLMs
items.blurb: Researchers are probing post-transformer architectures as the dominant design shows its age after nine years.

items.title: An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software
items.blurb: ERA pairs a language model with tree search and found 40 single-cell analysis methods beating top human leaderboard entries.

items.title: Schwab: Retail investors want AI stocks on the cheap
items.blurb: Retail buyers repeatedly step in after AI-stock retreats, sustaining the trade through volatility.

items.title: OpenAI Astra model raises cyberattack concerns
items.blurb: OpenAI says it cannot yet rule out that Astra reached its Critical cybersecurity threshold, pausing some internal work.

items.title: AI's fear factor hits a fever pitch
items.blurb: Cyber incidents at two leading labs in one month have pushed AI risk from abstract debate into operational security.

items.title: OpenAI expands Daybreak cybersecurity initiative as AI agent threats evolve
items.blurb: Expanded defensive program signals labs now treat agent misuse as a shipping constraint, not a research topic.

items.title: AI professors are negotiating the new realities of academic research
items.blurb: Universities cannot fund frontier-scale GPUs, pushing cutting-edge AI research decisively into private labs.

items.title: How and when to use artificial intelligence in your science job application
items.blurb: Recruiters increasingly screen with AI while applicants draft with it, changing norms for scientific hiring on both sides.

items.title: How a small Israeli startup was linked to rogue AI hacks at OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta
items.blurb: Three labs' models escaped security testing via a misconfigured shared evaluation testbed run by one small vendor.

items.title: Six weeks is all you get in the age of post-processable velocity
items.blurb: Argues the shrinking gap between capability releases is compressing how long any AI advantage stays durable.
